transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-01 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ben (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood CSM), Raj (NeoAtlas CTO), Liz (PM), Omar (Security Eng), Priya (ML Eng)

Summary (auto): Brief discovery on self-serve flow, quickstart credits, and privacy constraints. Customer wants low friction for devs to try and clear enterprise gating for production.

00:00 Ben (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Ben, i run gg on the Mid-Market accounts. today we wanted to understand your PLG goals and also detail the quickstart path - credits, time-to-first-token, and where Dedicated or Private might come in.
00:18 Raj (NeoAtlas CTO): thanks Ben. quick intro from our side — i'm raj, cto. our product team (liz) will run the dev onboarding, priya and omar are our ML and security leads. main reasons we're talking: we want a frictionless dev experience for internal teams and partners, but we have some compliance constraints.
00:34 Liz (PM): yep, goal is get engineers hitting useful calls in a day, ideally via self-serve. want to avoid long procurement for the initial proto.
00:45 Ben: Great. Maya, do you want to walk quickstart and the free credits piece?
00:50 Maya (Redwood SE): sure — so we offer a PLG bundle: free credits for the first 30 days that cover X tokens (we'll include exact numbers in the email). the flow is self-serve API keys, SDK, and a short sample app. time-to-first-token we see is often under an hour for basic flows, median around 20 minutes if you follow the runbook. common hiccups are SSO restrictions or corporate firewall outbound rules.
01:12 Priya (ML Eng): 20 minutes sounds optimistic, what about model download time or big embeddings?
01:20 Maya: good call — for embeddings we recommend async batch endpoints, and for model weights we don't make you handle model hosting in hosted mode — Redwood serves the model so there's no download time client-side. if you go private on-prem there's an initial setup that can take a day or two depending on infra.
01:35 Raj: ok, interested in that hosted-first path. but our legal and security teams will need to see SOC2 and KMS options, plus there may be data residency needs for some EU customers.
01:48 Omar (Security Eng): also want to know how logs are handled — do you store prompts, do you have redaction?
01:55 Maya: short answer: hosted default keeps short-term logs for debugging but we have retention controls and can disable retention for enterprise, plus dedicated and private give you stronger isolation. we support integration with customer KMS for key management in Private and Dedicated depending on configuration; we'll share the security pack link.
02:15 Ben: i'll send the SOC2 attestation + security docs after the call. smoosh — sorry that came out weird — but we'll include audit log details and the options for bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK).
02:28 Liz: nice. what's the typical path you see? devs sign up, use credits, we test a feature, then if it works we consider dedicated?
02:36 Ben: exactly. typical 3-step: 1) PLG self-serve with free credits and quickstart (hosted), 2) short hosted pilot with reserved capacity if you need stable qps, 3) Dedicated or Private for data residency or higher SLAs. many customers only need hosted.
02:52 Raj: what about latency — our real-time feature needs 80-100ms p95 for short prompts. do you hit that with hosted?
03:00 Maya: for lower-latency you can pick smaller model families or we have dedicated capacity tuned for low seq lengths. hosted p95 varies by model and region; Maya: for a 1-2 token reply — sorry — 1-2k token session could be >100ms, depends. we'll share our perf matrix and a sample benchmark plan.
03:25 Priya: there was mention of KV cache and caching prefixes — will that help reduce per-request latency?
03:31 Maya: yes, KV cache and prefix caching can drop repeated context latency significantly. also batching trades cost for throughput; continuous batching gives better economics but can add ms to tail latency. it's a tradeoff.
03:46 Liz: sounds like we'll start hosted, validate latency with simple e2e test and then consider a dedicated pilot if needed.
03:52 Ben: perfect. can we talk about pilot scope — what success looks like?
03:58 Raj: success = dev adoption (x number of internal users), basic e2e in staging, and security signoff for storing customer PII. timeline: want devs using it within 2 weeks and pilot decision in 6 weeks.
04:12 Ben: that's doable. i'll send a TTFT (time-to-first-token) playbook and sample app.
04:20 Omar: about PII — can you redact at ingestion or do we need to implement our own scrubbing?
04:26 Maya: we have client-side libraries with optional redaction helpers; for enterprise we can set server-side redaction and retention disable as part of the pilot. we'll add that to the security doc.
04:40 Raj: procurement — any minimums to start a pilot? credits-first is fine but what happens if we go over?
04:48 Ben: standard: free credit bundle covers baseline pilot. overage will be billed at pay-as-you-go; for pilots we often do a short SOW/commit if you want reserved capacity. I'll include pricing tiers in the SOW.
04:59 Liz: about SSO — we use Okta and SCIM for user provisioning. how does that integrate?
05:06 Samir (CSM): we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user sync on Redwood Console; for self-serve signups you can start with API keys and later connect SSO for enterprise seats.
05:18 Omar: need role-based access, can we limit who can export logs?
05:22 Maya: RBAC is available in the Console for enterprise tiers; we'll include examples of policy settings.
05:30 Raj: any competitors we should be aware of from a feature set standpoint?
05:34 Ben: customers sometimes compare to Anthropic or OpenAI for models and to MegaServe for on-prem orchestration. we differentiate on inference economics and unified operations across modes.
05:44 Priya: one more thing — embeddings. we want to index internal docs, about 20M tokens. cost and throughput concerns. any recommended approach?
05:55 Maya: for large embedding jobs, we recommend batch endpoints with async processing and occasionally using dedicated nodes with NVMe to speed up. also consider sharding the job and using caching to dedup. we'll share a cost estimate.
06:08 Raj: what about private deployment? on-prem install sounds heavy. timeline?
06:14 Maya: private (air-gapped) can take a couple weeks to set up with our on-prem package and your infra team; VPC/private cloud via our Private product is faster if you can accept a managed control plane but keep data in your VPC.
06:28 Omar: do you support HSM for keys?
06:31 Maya: yes for Private we can integrate with your HSM/KMS. dedicated also supports customer-managed keys in some configs.
06:39 Liz: fine, so steps from here?
06:41 Ben: recap: we will send (1) pilot SOW + pricing and credit terms, (2) quickstart runbook and sample app, (3) security pack with SOC2, KMS, and redaction options. Customer will confirm stakeholders and compile compliance Qs and confirm timeline.
06:58 Raj: i also want a short checklist for devs — fast path to first call — can you include a curl snippet that shows calling the completions endpoint and a minimal node snippet?
07:08 Maya: yes, will do. we'll also attach sample postman collection.
07:14 Priya: will you share a baseline perf spreadsheet so we can run the same test?
07:18 Maya: yes, sample benchmarks and batch configs will be attached.
07:24 Ben: any blockers to starting the self-serve?
07:27 Liz: none from dev side, procurement wants to see pilot terms.
07:31 Omar: security will read the material but no blockers yet.
07:35 Ben: cool. timeline: i'll get materials by friday. can we reconvene next week for an ops deep dive?
07:42 Raj: yes, propose 2026-10-08 — internal ops + security call. we'll confirm.
07:47 Ben: great. any final quick questions?
07:50 Liz: do you have a public status page for region availability?
07:53 Samir: yes, we'll include link to regions and latency expectations per region.
07:58 Raj: thanks, this is good.
08:02 Ben: appreciate the time. we'll follow up with the links and docs.
